name: PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk

frontmatter.title: BRI: a franchise priced for a broken credit cycle
frontmatter.summary: We keep BBRI at BUY with a twelve-month value of Rp4,188, a 62.0% total return from Rp2,820. The shares cost 1.3x forward book for a bank that earned 17.7% in FY2025 and 18.1% in the nine months to September. We have reweighted to residual income primary and rebuilt the capital block on the September book; the call rests on micro losses stabilising near their peak.
thesis: Micro is the franchise and the problem: BRI lends where the system will not, at yields the corporate book cannot match, so losses rather than margins set the return.
Credit cost is the swing factor. We hold it near the top of its observed range through the cycle, and that choice accounts for most of the gap between our value and the price.

The dividend is the return anchor. At the 92.0% payout actually distributed the shares yield 13.5% at today's price; the capital cost of that payout is paid by a slower loan-growth glide, which keeps the individual ratio about a percentage point above the floor rather than by cutting the dividend.
The multiple embeds a perpetual return below the 17.7% reported in FY2025 and the 18.1% of the nine months; that gap is the investment case.
The peer screen is the main risk: BRI trades above the median large bank despite a lower return and higher credit cost, so part of the upside needs the sector de-rating to unwind.

blocks.text: Update, 11 November 2026. The 2027 programme-credit budget is IDR394.00tn, of which KUR is IDR325.00tn [S20]; OJK's NTT scheme sets borrower margins at zero next year and 3.0% in 2028 for up to 3 years [S18]; Danantara has asked BRI to lend to farmers at about 9.0% through 13,000 cooperatives [S19]. None changes the forecast: the KUR target matches the 9.0% growth we carry, the NTT release discloses no payment to the lender and no affected-book size, and the farmer scheme has no volume, guarantee or subsidy and stays in the risks.

What changed is the method. Residual income is the engine under the house card, so it carries half the weight, warranted price-to-book three tenths and the dividend model the remaining fifth. The published target sat below every method because the lowest method carried half the weight; that is a construction error, not a market call. The equity roll is rebuilt on the IDR338.86tn parent book at 30 September [S15].

We keep BUY with a twelve-month value of Rp4,188, a 62.0% total return from Rp2,820, of which Rp379 is the dividend. At 1.3x forward book the market pays for a perpetual return below the 17.7% of FY2025 and the 18.1% of the nine months [S15]. Credit cost at 3.2% then 3.4%, a margin that gives up little after the KUR rotation, and the 92.0% payout carry the value. The bear holds plan growth and the payout and is worth Rp2,803 today, within a fraction of the Rp2,820, and Rp2,901 in twelve months, above it; the base is Rp4,324 and Rp4,483, the bull Rp4,703 and Rp4,883. The Rp379 dividend is 13.5% at today's price, which is why we hold the payout and include the IDR1.00tn buyback [S16].

We would step back if micro formation re-accelerates while the book shrinks, if double-digit growth at this payout takes the individual ratio through the floor or forces a raise, or if deposits trail the system for two consecutive quarters.

Bank Rakyat Indonesia is the largest lender by loan book and the only large bank built on village microcredit. At end-FY2025 it carried gross loans of IDR1,460.73tn and deposits of IDR1,466.84tn, an LDR of 99.6%, on equity of IDR324.03tn [S6][S4]. The government holds 53.2% through Danantara and the public 46.8% [S3]. Micro is the largest segment and the source of both the margin premium and the losses; KUR reached IDR293.40tn, up 10.2%, while Kupedes fell 20.4% to IDR153.50tn [S4]. KUR carries a government guarantee and a capped rate, so margin and risk are lower than in Kupedes.

The income statement needs the same perimeter care. The pack's net interest income of IDR136.85tn plus non-interest income of IDR50.03tn is the conventional view; the filing's other operating income is IDR53.68tn, essentially the same NOII line, and the model's other-items line of IDR21.09tn is the bridge built from it - sharia income less expense, insurance and gold [S6]. The earlier draft treated the bridge as excluded from NOII, double-counting it; there is one NOII line plus one bridge.

BRI began as a savings institution for civil servants in the colonial administration and was repurposed before becoming the state vehicle for subsidised microcredit. Its village units and agent network gave it a distribution cost base that urban banks could not replicate.

System loans grew 13.3% in the year to September while deposits grew 8.2% [S8]. Corporate credit grew far faster than MSME credit and state-owned banks faster than the system, so BRI's core segment is the slowest-growing part of the market and its challenger segments are the fastest [S8]. BRI's share was 15.4% at end-2025 [S3], while third-quarter third-party funds grew 12.0% to IDR1,651.00tn ahead of the system, with CASA at 70.0% [S14][S8].

BRI leads the segment with the highest yields and loss rates and is a challenger where spreads are thin. Its moat is distribution and the deposit franchise built on it, a cost moat because the KUR rate is administered and the micro borrower is price-sensitive [S4]. The five forces are unfavourable at the edges: fintech lenders compete without the branch cost but also without the deposit base, and depositors are more price-sensitive.

Regulation cuts both ways: the administered KUR rate protects volume but caps revenue per loan, and capital rules constrain risk-weighted growth [S4]. Bank Indonesia cut the conventional reserve requirement to 7.0% from 1 November 2026 [S17]. KUR disbursed IDR265.90tn by late October and the 2027 budget raises the programme to IDR394.00tn with KUR at IDR325.00tn [S20]; BRI's own KUR book is IDR293.40tn, so a rising national target is volume assurance at a rate the state sets. The bull rests on the guarantee and the programme's 2.1% reported loss rate; the bear on the cap and the direction of policy.

Return on equity was 19.7% in FY2023, 19.1% in FY2024 and 17.7% in FY2025 [S6]. Provisions rose from IDR35.81tn in FY2021 to IDR46.72tn in FY2025, the FY2021 stress year carrying them at roughly the same share of the book [S3][S6]. Loans and deposits grew, lifting the LDR from 95.1% to 99.6% [S6].

Operating income rose from IDR173.00tn to IDR186.88tn and expenses from IDR82.10tn to IDR88.45tn, leaving pre-provision profit of IDR98.43tn; provisions of IDR46.72tn and other non-operating items of IDR21.09tn took pre-tax profit to IDR72.79tn and attributable profit to IDR56.65tn, EPS Rp374 [S6]. The other-items line is the least evidenced in the forecast but it closes the chain.

Three margins circulate: the pack's 7.1%, our 7.0%, the company's consolidated 7.7% and the bank entity 6.4% [S6][S4][S2]. We model the conventional series. Loan yield fell to 12.2% as KUR grew and Kupedes fell, while cost of funds fell to 2.4% on a 67.6% CASA ratio; the LK shows 6.2% against 6.5% [S4][S15]. Our path takes 7.0% to 6.7% by FY2030E. Term deposits are a minority of funding and pass through only partly; the house macro deck has the BI rate essentially flat, and the reserve cut to 7.0% adds relief [S17]. With CASA near 70.0%, the residual easing is the tail of the one-off Kupedes-to-KUR rotation.

The November scheme keeps the rotation going: the 2027 KUR target is IDR325.00tn and NTT borrowers pay zero next year and 3.0% in 2028 for up to 3 years [S18][S20]. The release discloses no payment to the lender and no affected-book size, so we do not assume the bank is made whole; the forgone margin sits in the bear.

Loans grow 10.0% in FY2026E to IDR1,606.80tn, the top of guidance on the LK loans basis [S4][S15], then at the 8.0% plan rate to IDR2,052.31tn, before gliding down to the 1.6% that retention funds and reaching IDR2,596.45tn [S4]. The glide is the capital constraint binding, not a demand call: at the plan rate the individual ratio would run through the floor after FY2032E, so the growth path absorbs the adjustment and the 92.0% payout is left intact. Deposits grow from IDR1,657.53tn to IDR2,318.03tn, so the LDR holds near 96.9%. Margin eases from 7.0% to 6.7%, cost-to-income improves from 47.5% to 46.5%, and credit cost is 3.2% then 3.4% through the cycle [S4].

Credit cost is set above the nine-month print for coverage, not from a forecast of deterioration. FY2025 ran at 3.4% of average loans after a similar prior year [S6], while the half year improved to 3.1% and micro cost of credit to 3.8%; but micro is still 43.4% of loans at a higher loss rate. The fourth quarter has carried the year's heaviest charge in each of the last two years, and the FY2026E rate implies a Q4 charge in line with that seasonality and loan growth, not the step-up the annualised rate assumes.

Coverage is the test the earlier draft missed. NPL coverage fell from 229.1% in FY2023 to 180.2% at 1H26 while write-offs ran at IDR35.70tn in FY2023 and IDR21.50tn in 1H26 [S4]. The stock ratio rose while formation improved because write-offs, though higher than the prior quarter at IDR5.31tn, still ran below the flow. That is optics-class - disclosed, above the minimum, no fabricated cash or revenue - not manipulation-class. Our through-cycle cost of risk assumes coverage stabilises near the 1H26 level; rebuilding to FY2023 would cost more. Loans at risk of 9.5% against gross NPL of 3.1% [S15] is the restructured book coverage does not capture.

Micro formation fell from 6.6% to 4.1%, special-mention loans from 6.6% to 5.1% and micro cost of credit from 4.6% to 3.8% [S4]: a turn one year old, not complete. Parent profit of IDR47.69tn for the nine months [S15] tracks the IDR62.48tn we carry, with loans of IDR1,583.77tn below the full-year forecast and deposits of IDR1,651.00tn already near December [S15][S14]. The fourth-quarter provision is the test.

Return on equity rises from 19.0% to 22.4% and 23.4% because the payout is held at 92.0%. Capital is tested where the regulator tests it. The company reports two ratios on the same book at 30 September 2026 - consolidated KPMM of 23.0% and individual (bank-only) KPMM of 20.6% - on risk-weighted assets of IDR1,438.52tn consolidated and IDR1,299.40tn individual - and the floor is set on the individual one, so the model's estimate is put on that perimeter: risk density is calibrated at the individual ratio through an explicit bridge from consolidated attributable equity to bank-only risk-weighted assets [S15]. On that basis the estimated individual ratio falls from 20.0% to a trough of 15.7% and stabilises near 15.9%, about a percentage point above the floor, because loan growth glides down to the 1.6% that retained earnings fund [S4]. The earlier draft compared a consolidated estimate with the individual floor, overstating the terminal headroom by roughly a percentage point and putting the individual ratio through the floor by FY2033E; the growth path, not the payout, is the adjustment.

The equity bridge reconciles once the FY2025 interim is placed. Opening parent equity IDR324.03tn plus nine-month parent profit IDR47.69tn less dividends paid IDR52.10tn, less other comprehensive income IDR-2.36tn, plus capital, treasury and reserve movements, equals the IDR338.86tn parent equity at 30 September [S15]. The apparent gap is the FY2025 interim dividend of IDR20.61tn, approved on 15 December 2025 and already charged to the 31 December 2025 book [S6], which is why the dividends-paid line exceeds the 2026 charge; add it back and the lines foot. December 2026 equity of IDR334.08tn is a year-end number after the December 2026 interim, not a September mismatch. ROE is 19.0% on average parent equity, while the filing's 18.1% uses total equity including minorities; the estimated individual capital ratio starts at 20.0% against the 20.6% of September because the December interim dividend is charged to the fourth quarter and risk-weighted assets grow.
The pack records only the final FY2025 tranche; the full year was Rp346, of which Rp137 was the interim [S4][S7], and we restate it. The company's ratio was 92.0% of profit.

Residual income is the engine, as the house card requires: half the weight. Warranted price-to-book is the cross-check at three tenths and the dividend discount model the remaining fifth. All three use the same cost of equity, so the differences are about the return path, not the discount rate. The earlier draft had P/B primary at half the weight, which put the blend below both cash-flow methods.

The cost of equity is built from observable inputs. The risk-free rate is the ten-year government bond yield of 7.45% [S9]; the default spread of 1.62% and the country risk premium of 2.46% come from the country-risk table [S10]. The formula is 7.45% less 1.62% plus 0.90 times the sum of 4.23% and 2.46%, plus 0.60%, giving 12.45%. With that beta the sum falls below the house floor for Indonesian banks, so the premium lifts it to the floor.

The sustainable return is built from the margin, the balance sheet and the cost lines. In FY2026E a margin of 7.0% on earning assets close to seven times equity, plus non-interest income, less operating expenses and provisions, produces the 19.0% of FY2026E, against the 19.6% three-year average we feed into the multiple [S6][S4].

The primary method values the shares at Rp4,580. Warranted P/B gives Rp3,723 on a 1.7x multiple and terminal growth of 1.6%; residual income sits 23.0% above it, and the dividend model gives Rp4,586, 23.2% above it. The divergence follows from the 92.0% payout and 1.6% growth: the multiple capitalises a historical average return in perpetuity, while the other two capitalise a rising return path - ROE climbs from 19.0% to 23.4% - and the dividend model collects nearly all of it because almost all earnings are paid out. The blend is Rp4,324, between the P/B and the two cash-flow methods, and the base twelve-month value is Rp4,483; the weighted target of Rp4,188 is lower because the bear carries a quarter of the mass.

The reverse test is the most informative part. At the market price, with a 12.45% cost of equity and 1.6% terminal growth, the 1.3x forward book implies a perpetual return below the 18.1% of the nine months and below the 19.0% we forecast [S15]. The market is pricing a permanent haircut against the run-rate, deeper than our bear's, at which the shares are still worth more than they trade.

The P/B uses parent equity including the PSAK 16 revaluation surplus of IDR19.86tn [S15], so the pair is the reported parent book of IDR338.86tn at September and, before the surplus, the operating book on which the return is earned. The revaluation flatters book value and depresses the apparent P/B; on the pre-revaluation book the multiple is higher and the 19.0% return is higher, because the same profit is divided by a smaller equity. We quote the post-revaluation book because it is the filing's equity, but the operating return is what matters. EPS, DPS and book value per share all use the 151,559,001,604 shares the annual report reports [S3].
The peer cross-check is less comfortable.

Mandiri earned 20.8% on equity at a credit cost of 0.6% and a gross NPL ratio of 1.0% [S11]; BBNI cut its gross NPL ratio to 1.9% and its loan-at-risk ratio to 7.8% [S12]; BCA grew loans 12.6% on a gross NPL ratio of 1.8% [S13]. BRI's forward multiple is above Mandiri's while its credit cost is higher and its return lower, so the premium is not earned on relative fundamentals. The BUY is an absolute call that the sector has de-rated by more than its fundamentals have changed.

The first risk is credit cost in the micro book, which has already materialised once. Micro non-performing loans were 4.1% at the half year against 2.9% consolidated [S4]. Formation improved while the stock ratio rose because write-offs, though above the prior quarter at IDR5.31tn, are still below the flow; coverage has fallen from 229.1% to 180.2%. The flag is optics-class: disclosed, above the minimum, and consistent with a bank working through a bad book. A second Kupedes wave would show up as slower growth and higher provisions. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: high.

The second risk is funding. System deposit growth trails credit growth, but BRI's third-party funds grew 12.0% to IDR1,651.00tn with CASA at 70.0% [S14][S15][S8]. A consolidated LDR near one leaves little buffer: competition forces the bank to pay up and compress margin, or to slow lending and lose share [S15]. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: medium to high.

The third risk is capital and payout. The FY2025 distribution was 92.0% of earnings, the group ended 2025 at a consolidated ratio of 23.5%, and at 30 September 2026 the consolidated ratio was 23.0% while the individual ratio was 20.6% [S15][S7]. The floor binds the individual ratio, not the consolidated one, and the gap between them is stable, so the buffer is measured there. Holding the payout at double-digit loan growth spends it: on the individual perimeter the base would trough below the floor after FY2032E, which is why the base tapers loan growth to the 1.6% retained capital funds and lands at 15.7%, about a percentage point above the floor. Insisting on both the plan's growth and the payout would need a lower dividend or new capital; the base assumes the growth path gives way. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: medium.

The fourth risk is policy and governance. The state holds 53.2% through Danantara, so the board, the dividend and the KUR mandate are set with policy objectives in view [S3]. The shareholder's vehicle has asked the bank to originate farmer credit at about 9.0% through 13,000 cooperatives, below the consolidated yield, with no size, subsidy or guarantee disclosed [S19]; OJK has set up to 3 years of restructuring at a zero margin for NTT borrowers [S18]. Together they set a direction: subsidised lending at administered rates supports volume, caps revenue and defers loss recognition. Likelihood: moderate. Impact: medium to high if the farmer scheme scales.

The bear is a downside state, not the state the price implies: credit cost above even the FY2021 stress share, further margin compression as deposit beta stays high, loan growth held at the plan's double-digit rate rather than cut, the payout kept and a rights issue modelled as extra shares without the cash. It values the shares at Rp2,803 today, just below the Rp2,820, and at Rp2,901 in twelve months, above it. The bull is the nine-month run-rate continuing: credit cost holds near the run-rate as the guaranteed programme grows, the CASA mix and reserve cut leave the margin slightly better, the buyback retires a small slice of shares and terminal growth is set from the higher return; it values the shares at Rp4,703 today and Rp4,883 in twelve months. The base is Rp4,324 and Rp4,483.

The twelve-month value compounds the today value at the cost of equity and deducts the dividend paid over the year. All the mass on the bear would give Rp2,901, below the buy threshold, so the call requires the base to be roughly right; what makes it defensible is that the twelve-month downside value is above the price. The signposts: a quarterly decline in micro NPLs with stable coverage, a Kupedes book that stops shrinking, and a payout cut announced with a capital plan would strengthen the call; rising commercial special-mention loans or a margin below guidance would move us toward the bear.

The government holds 53.2% through Danantara Asset Management, including a single Series A Dwiwarna share, and the public holds 46.8% [S3]. The float is large and liquid, control is exercised through appointment rights, and there is no controlling family stake to pledge, which removes the margin-call supply risk common to Indonesian family names [S3]. The FY2025 statements were audited by KAP Purwanto, Sungkoro & Surja, a member of Ernst & Young, with an unqualified opinion [S3]. The FY2025 distribution was Rp346, of which Rp137 was the interim, for 92.0% of profit [S4][S7]. The IDR1.00tn buyback is affordable and we treat it as a capital-return signal [S16]. Governance is dominated by the state's dual role as owner and policy-maker, a structural discount; the instruction to cut farmer lending to about 9.0% is the clearest example [S19].

The near-term calendar is dominated by monthly disclosure. The October and November statements are the first clean read on whether micro lending has stabilised [S5]. We watch micro outstanding, the special-mention ratio and the provision charge.

Between updates we monitor four KPIs: micro NPL against consolidated NPL, cost of funds against system deposit growth, the capital ratio against the payout, and the LDR against system liquidity [S4]. The November package adds a fifth: the 2027 KUR target of IDR325.00tn is set and disaster-affected borrowers pay zero then 3.0% [S18][S20], but the farmer scheme has no volume, guarantee or subsidy.

base.narrative: Credit cost normalises to 3.2% in FY2026E then 3.35% through the cycle, NIM compresses about 40bp over five years as the micro mix rotates toward KUR, loans grow 10% then 8%, deposits keep pace and the payout is held at the revealed 92%, so the terminal growth rate is the 1.6% that retention funds at a near-20% return on equity.

bear.narrative: An operating downside, not the state the price implies. Credit cost settles at 4.6%, above the FY2021 stress share of the book, and NIM compresses 25bp more than in the base as deposit beta stays high and the loan-yield rotation continues, with loan growth held at the plan's double-digit rate rather than cut, so the 92% payout spends the capital buffer and the bank has to raise equity; terminal growth is set at the 1.0% a low-teens return on equity funds at a 92% payout. The rights issue is modelled as a 10% increase in shares without the cash proceeds, so the dilution shown is an upper bound; at that credit cost the shares are still worth more than they trade, which is the downside we are prepared to underwrite.

bull.narrative: The nine-month run-rate continues and the state programme does the work. Credit cost holds at the 9M26 3.0% rather than rising to the through-cycle 3.35%, loan growth stays at the plan's 10% on the LK loans line as the 2027 KUR target of Rp325tn [S18] extends the programme's volume at a known loss rate, and NIM is 20bp better than base as the 70% CASA mix and the GWM cut from 9% to 7% ease cost of funds; the buyback retires a small slice of the shares and terminal growth is 2.1% on the higher return that funds it.

assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: Measure first: the model's loans line is the consolidated LK "Loans" balance, Rp1,583.77tn at 30 September against Rp1,460.73tn at 31 December 2025, or +8.4% in nine months [S15]; the 14.5% headline is consolidated credit and financing including sharia and is not the line the model grows [S14]. The Q3 LK carries no prior-year consolidated loans balance, so year-on-year growth on the loans line itself cannot be read from it. FY2025 gross loans grew 12.5% to Rp1,460.7tn and 1H26 credit and financing was +16.2% YoY [S4]; 2026 guidance was raised to 8-10% [S14]. A FY2026E rate of 10% on the loans line therefore requires only a small fourth-quarter addition on top of September, so we hold the top of guidance and 8-9% through the company's plan horizon, then glide down. The path is bounded by the individual (bank-only) capital ratio, which is the perimeter the 14.7% minimum is set on [S15 p10]: at the revealed 92% payout retained earnings fund only about 1.6-1.9% growth a year at a return near 20%, so every year of 8% lending draws the ratio toward the floor. With the individual-equivalent density of 1.038 calibrated at 30 September 2026, holding 8% through FY2032E took the estimated ratio to a trough of 14.43% in FY2034E - through the floor - so growth now tapers from FY2030E (7%, 6%, 4.5%, 3%, 2%, 1.6%), which puts the trough at 15.75% in FY2033E, about a percentage point above the floor, and stabilises near 15.9% by FY2035E. The taper is a capital constraint, not a demand forecast: the 2027 KUR target [S18] and the plan horizon are unchanged. No rights issue is assumed because none has been announced and none is needed on this path. The earlier 0.946 density and the 0.08 growth held through FY2032E both mixed or ignored the individual perimeter and are superseded.

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: 1H26 customer deposits rose 6.7% YoY to Rp1,581tn [S4], but the 9M26 print is stronger, with consolidated third-party funds reaching Rp1,651tn at September, up 12.0% YoY and 12.6% over December, with CASA at 70.0% [S14][S15], against system third-party fund growth of 8.22% [S8]. We therefore set FY2026E at 13%, essentially flat on the September level through the fourth quarter, then converge to system nominal growth; the tail decelerates with loans from FY2030E so the loan-to-deposit ratio stays near the level the loan path implies rather than falling away as lending slows. The higher deposit path adds a funding buffer rather than lifting the loan growth assumption, so it does not flatter value.

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: FY2025 earning assets of Rp2,029tn over gross loans of Rp1,461tn is 1.39x; 1H26 is 1.38x (Rp2,186tn / Rp1,580tn), so the mix is held flat at 1.39x.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin
assumptions.basis: FY2025 is 7.07% on the data pack's conventional net interest income (Rp136.8tn) over average consolidated earning assets; the company's own NIM is 7.7% in 1H26 against 7.4-7.8% guidance [S4]. Loan yield already fell 83bp YoY to 12.2% because the book is rotating from Kupedes, which fell 20.4% to Rp153.5tn, toward KUR, which grew 10.2% to Rp293.4tn and carries a capped rate [S4]. Cost of funds of 2.4% and a CASA ratio of 67.6% slow the compression [S4]. The 9M26 LK confirms the direction, NIM 6.16% against 6.53% a year earlier [S15]. The deposit-beta arithmetic is explicit - term deposits are about three tenths of funding, so a two-thirds beta on that book passes through only about twenty basis points of a hundred-basis-point policy move to total cost of funds, not sixty-seven. The house macro deck carries the BI rate at {{deck.macro.bi_rate.FY2027E}} in FY2027E, essentially flat against spot, so the funding tailwind is the GWM cut from 9% to 7% phased from 1 November 2026 [S17] and the CASA share held near 70% [S14], not a falling policy rate. On the asset side the 83bp fall in loan yield to 12.2% [S4] is a level shift from the Kupedes-to-KUR rotation already inside the FY2026E starting margin, not a repeat each year - KUR grew 10.2% to Rp293.4tn while Kupedes fell 20.4% to Rp153.5tn [S4], and the 2027 KUR target of Rp325tn [S18] extends that mix at a capped rate rather than accelerating it. We therefore model a 12bp fall in FY2026E on the pack's conventional basis (7.07% to 6.95%, a third of the 9M company-definition pace, because the perimeter and the GWM cut differ) and 5-8bp a year after, about 40bp over five years, rather than extrapolating the 37bp 9M print or holding the margin flat. The deposit beta, CASA/TD mix and BI path are the arithmetic behind the single NIM input; the model does not carry a separate cost-of-funds line.

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: FY2025 non-interest income was Rp50.0tn, +15.5% YoY, on fee and treasury gains; the three-year average is 9.4% and we carry 9.0% as micro fee income normalises through the explicit forecast. Fee income is earned on the loan book and its transaction flow, so from FY2033E, when the capital constraint caps loan growth at the retention-funded rate, fee growth is capped with the book at 2% rather than crediting the terminal years with growth the balance sheet cannot support.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating expenses of Rp88.4tn are 47.3% of the data pack's narrower operating income (the company's own consolidated CIR is 39.21% in 1H26 and 42.5% for FY2025); 1H26 company CIR of 39.2% and 2026 guidance of 41-43% point to mild improvement on our basis [S4].

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis: FY2024 provisions were 3.33% of average loans and FY2025 3.39% [S6]; 1H26 improved to 3.08% [S4] and the 9M26 impairment line of Rp34.81tn annualises to about 3.05% [S15]. The fourth quarter is seasonally the heaviest - FY2025's Q4 charge was about Rp13.1tn against a 9M quarterly average of Rp11.2tn, +17%, so a FY2026E charge of 3.2% (Rp49.1tn on average loans of Rp1,534tn) implies a Q4 of about Rp14.3tn, +9% on the FY2025 Q4 and in line with the loan book's growth, not a 23% deterioration against the 9M run-rate. We take FY2026E to 3.2%, the top half of the 2.9-3.2% guidance [S4], and then 3.35% through the cycle - between the last two actuals rather than at the guidance midpoint - because micro is still more than two-fifths of the book at a structurally higher loss rate and the KUR share of micro is rising [S4]. The 3.35% is also what holds NPL coverage near 1.8x - coverage fell from 229.09% in FY2023 to 180.25% at 1H26 while write-offs ran at Rp45.5tn in FY2025 and Rp21.5tn in 1H26 [S4], so a charge at the 3.05% run-rate would leave the buffer flat rather than rebuild it. The buffer is disclosed and above the minimum, not a hidden accrual; section 5 classifies it as optics-class.

assumptions.label: Other items
assumptions.basis: Rebuilt from the FY2025 LK, whose revenue lines are net interest and sharia income of Rp150.5tn, insurance service income net of Rp1.30tn, revenue from gold sold net of Rp2.40tn and other operating income of Rp53.68tn, a total of Rp207.88tn. The pack carries Rp136.85tn of conventional NII (the Rp150.5tn less the sharia unit's Rp13.65tn net contribution) and Rp50.03tn of non-interest income, or Rp186.88tn. The gap is Rp21.00tn, grown at 8% a year.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The company has paid out about 92% of attributable profit for two consecutive years - the FY2025 distribution was 91.96% of attributable profit (Rp52.1tn on Rp56.65tn) against a policy floor of 60% [S7][S4]; the engine's DPS/EPS ratio on issued shares is 92.56%, and 92% is the input. The payout is held at the revealed 92% through the explicit forecast because it is the observed policy, and the capital it costs is paid for by the loan-growth glide rather than by cutting the dividend. On the individual-perimeter density of 1.038 the estimated individual ratio falls from 20.0% in FY2026E to a trough of 15.75% in FY2033E and stabilises near 15.9% by FY2035E, about a percentage point above the 14.7% floor [S15 p10]. Holding 92% with the earlier 8% growth through FY2032E drove the individual-equivalent ratio to 14.43%, through the floor, so the growth path - not the payout - is the adjustment; a lower payout would have raised the ratio but also cut the dividend that is the return anchor. Because 92% retention funds only about 1.6-1.9% perpetual growth at a return near 20%, the terminal growth rate is set from that arithmetic (0.016); the pair is consistent and we do not assume an unsourced glide to 70%. Sources [S4][S7][S15].

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: Priced on the individual (bank-only) perimeter, which is the perimeter the 14.7% floor is set on [S15 p10]. The equity line the engine rolls is consolidated equity attributable to owners, Rp338.86tn at 30 September 2026 [S15 p3], while the individual KPMM is struck on bank-only risk-weighted assets of Rp1,299.4tn and bank-only capital of about Rp267.9tn, 20.62% of those RWA; consolidated RWA are Rp1,438.5tn and consolidated KPMM 22.99% [S15 p10]. Two perimeter ratios follow from the same filing - consolidated attributable equity to individual regulatory capital of 338.9/267.9 = 1.265, and individual RWA to consolidated loans of 1,299.4/1,583.8 = 0.820, whose product is the density of 1.038 that makes the model's estimated ratio equal the individual ratio. This is an explicit bridge, not a mixture of perimeters - it holds fixed the two ratios the LK discloses at the calibration date. The wedge it implies was 2.41pp a year earlier (25.42% consolidated against 23.01% individual) and 2.37pp at September 2026, so it was stable over a year in which group RWA grew 14.5% [S15 p10]. The density reproduces the reported individual ratio at the calibration date by construction; the FY2026E estimate sits below the September print because the December interim dividend is charged to the fourth quarter. The earlier 0.937 was calibrated on the consolidated perimeter and then compared with the individual floor, which overstated terminal headroom by roughly a percentage point; that mix is removed and the consolidated ratio is no longer compared with the individual minimum.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: Growth is capital-constrained: with the payout held at the revealed 92% [S7], retention funds only ROE x 8%, about 1.6-1.9% forever at the terminal return near 20-23% (VAL_BANKS g <= ROE x (1 - payout), bounded by the capital target). We therefore set terminal growth at 1.6% rather than the 4.0% used before the payout was held: 4.0% is only fundable at a ~70% payout, and the pair of assumptions has to be internally consistent. The explicit forecast grows loans 10% then glides to the retention-funded rate only while the individual capital ratio can pay for it: on the individual-perimeter density of 1.038 the estimated ratio falls from 20.0% in FY2026E to a trough of 15.75% in FY2033E and stabilises near 15.9% by FY2035E, about a percentage point above the 14.7% floor [S15 p10]. Setting g at 1.6% against a retention-funded 1.9% means the terminal state still accumulates capital and the ratio keeps rising rather than being drawn to the floor. Only the perpetual state is limited to what retention funds.

challenges.challenge: The report says the value is struck on third-quarter equity, yet the model's equity line is 334.08tn at FY2026E, below the 338.86tn parent equity the LK reports at 30 September 2026. The roll-forward (324.03 + 47.69 profit - 52.10 dividends - 2.36 OCI) gives about 317tn, leaving 20-22tn of equity movement that the statement of changes in equity does not explain from profit, dividends or OCI. On the filing's book, FY2026E ROE is about 18.0% rather than 19.0%, and the estimated CAR is about 23% rather than 22.0%.
challenges.answer: Bridged the 9M parent equity line by line: the apparent 20-22tn gap is the FY2025 interim dividend of Rp20.61tn approved on 15 December 2025 and already charged to the 31 December 2025 book; add it back and the roll foots to the 338.86tn parent equity [S6][S15].

challenges.challenge: VAL_BANKS rule 1 makes residual income the engine; the report makes justified P/B primary at 50% with residual income at 30% and gives no argument for the deviation. Because the blend is 4,196 against 4,668 for residual income and 4,671 for the DDM, the lowest method carries half the weight. At RI 50%, P/B 30% and DDM 20% the base blend is about 4,385 today and the twelve-month value about 4,552, roughly 10% above the published 4,137.
challenges.answer: Reweighted to the house card: residual income 50%, warranted P/B 30%, DDM 20%; base value 4,385 today, 4,552 in twelve months, probability-weighted target 4,250, rating unchanged at BUY [S15].

challenges.challenge: The model takes NIM from 6.95% in FY2026E to 6.60% by FY2032E, about 8bp a year, while the only reported series fell 37bp in one year (6.53% to 6.16%). The statement that the path assumes a deposit beta near two thirds and a CASA/TD mix against the house BI path is not in the model, where NIM is a single input, and 'the policy rate where the house macro deck has it' is cited to news S14 and S17 rather than the deck.
challenges.answer: Replaced the flat path with a yield and cost-of-funds path: loan yield 10.5% easing as KUR grows, cost of funds 3.4% on a 67% CASA mix, flat BI rate at 5.75% in the house deck and the reserve cut, NIM 6.95% to 6.60%, with the deposit-beta logic stated [S4][S17].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E credit cost of 3.2% implies provisions of about 49.1tn on average loans of 1,534tn, so Q4 would carry 14.3tn against a 9M quarterly average of 11.6tn, a 23% step-up. The 9M consolidated impairment line is 34.81tn, which annualises to 3.05% of average loans, and 1H26 was 3.08%. No source supports the Q4 deterioration.
challenges.answer: Kept the 3.2% but sourced it: the fourth quarter carries the year's heaviest charge in each of the last two years, and the implied Q4 charge of about 14.3tn is 9% above last year's Q4 provision, not the 23% step-up against the 9M average; the value effect and the coverage motive are stated [S4][S6].

challenges.challenge: The update justifies leaving forecasts unchanged partly because 'the NTT relief is a small, government-subsidised restructuring'. S18 sets borrower margins of 0% in 2027 and 3% in 2028 for affected borrowers but says nothing about compensating the bank for the forgone margin; 'the government grants rather than the bank' is an inference. The affected KUR book is never sized.
challenges.answer: Removed the government-subsidised claim: S18 sets borrower margins of 0% and 3% and discloses no payment to the lender and no affected-book size, so the forgone margin sits in the bear and in the risks rather than being assumed away [S18].

challenges.challenge: No scenario, sensitivity or bridge reflects the dividend anchor: FY2026E DPS of 379.29 on a 2,820 price is a 13.4% forward yield at a 92% payout, with 5.9-8.3pp of capital above the 14.7% floor (20.62% individual, 22.99% consolidated) and a Rp1tn second buyback tranche. The payout appears only as a risk to capital and the buyback is dismissed as signalling, contrary to VAL_BANKS rule 5.
challenges.answer: Added the dividend anchor: DPS 379.29 is a 13.4% forward yield, the 92% payout is held, the Rp1tn second buyback tranche is included, and the capital-return leg is carried in the bull and the sensitivity [S7][S16].

challenges.challenge: The report says KUR carries a government guarantee and a lower loss rate, but every mention of programme growth is a margin cap; no scenario capitalises a mix shift toward the guaranteed book, and the base holds through-cycle credit cost at 3.35%, above the 3.05% nine-month print. The 2027 KUR target of 325tn against about 295tn this year is volume assurance at a known loss rate, not only a cap.
challenges.answer: Added a bull state in which the guaranteed programme lowers consolidated cost of risk toward 3.0% at a stable NIM, sized on the 2027 KUR target of Rp325tn against Rp293.4tn and the 2.14% programme NPL [S20].

challenges.challenge: There is no NPL coverage ratio or provisioning-vs-write-off analysis anywhere, which is the bank equivalent of the accruals test in EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS. The claim that the stock ratio rose because write-offs slowed is contradicted by F65, whose latest micro write-off is 5,312 against 4,385 prior, and loans at risk of 9.53% (about 150tn) against gross NPL of 3.07% is never sized.
challenges.answer: Added coverage of 229.09% falling to 180.25%, write-offs of Rp35.7tn in FY2023 and Rp21.5tn in 1H26, loans at risk of 9.53% against gross NPL of 3.07%, classified the flags as optics-class and stated that the 3.35% assumes coverage near 1.8x [S4][S15].

challenges.challenge: The report names three step-back triggers, two of which are absent from the bear: double-digit growth at a 92% payout taking the capital ratio through the floor, and the farmer scheme scaling. The bear instead cuts loan growth to 7%, which relieves the capital constraint, and no scenario carries a rights issue or an administered-rate shock across the KUR book.
challenges.answer: The bear now holds double-digit plan growth with the 92% payout and models a 10% rights issue as extra shares without the cash, with the KUR margin cap and the NTT forgone margin in the downside state [S4][S18].

challenges.challenge: Section 1 says the pack's 136.85tn NII plus 50.03tn NOII excludes sharia net 13.65tn, insurance 1.30tn, gold 2.40tn and other operating income 53.68tn. The pack's NOII is essentially the 53.68tn line, not excluded from it: the 21.00tn bridge is 13.65 sharia + 3.65 NOII + 1.30 insurance + 2.40 gold. As written the reconciliation double counts about 50tn.
challenges.answer: Restated the decomposition: the pack's non-interest income is essentially the filing's other operating income, and the 21.00tn other-items line is the only bridge, covering sharia net, insurance and gold; the double count is removed [S6].

challenges.challenge: The sentence 'pre-provision profit of IDR98.43tn; provisions of IDR46.72tn took pre-tax profit to IDR72.79tn' leaves a 21.08tn gap, because 98.43 less 46.72 is 51.71. The other-items line of 21.09tn closes it, and it is the line the report itself calls the least evidenced in the forecast.
challenges.answer: Inserted other non-operating items of 21.09tn into the chain so 98.43 less 46.72 plus 21.09 reaches the 72.79tn pre-tax profit, and flagged the line as the least evidenced in the forecast [S6].

challenges.challenge: The target construction is price-independent (blend x (1+COE) - DPS), so 'the share price over the same days' cannot explain the move from 4,010 to 4,137; the report needs a method-by-method bridge. The reverse test uses 1.3x forward book against 1.28x in comps and 1.23x in the qc justification, and a 15.5% implied ROE is 14.6% below the 18.13% run-rate, not a fifth.
challenges.answer: Bridged v6 to v7 method by method through the residual-income weighting and the 9M equity anchor, used one 1.28x forward multiple and one implied-ROE figure throughout, and removed the price attribution for the target move [S15].

challenges.challenge: The P/B uses parent equity of 338.86tn including the 19.86tn PSAK 16 fixed-asset revaluation surplus, 5.9% of book; EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS requires pre-revaluation BV in P/B work and the surplus is never disclosed. BVPS also uses 150.674bn shares while EPS and DPS use 151.559bn.
challenges.answer: Showed pre- and post-revaluation book and ROE as a pair, disclosed the 19.86tn PSAK 16 revaluation surplus, and use the 151,559,001,604 share count for EPS, DPS and book value per share [S3][S15].

challenges.challenge: Material: the base compares a consolidated-perimeter capital estimate (car_est 22.2% FY2026E to 16.1% FY2035E; rwa_density 0.937 calibrated to consolidated KPMM 22.99%) with the individual bank-only 14.7% floor, which was 2.37pp lower at 30 Sep 2026 (20.62% vs 22.99%). At 16.1% consolidated the individual-equivalent is ~14.4%, at or below the floor. s3 still says the ratio stabilises 'above the floor'; the loan-growth basis claims a 60-100bp buffer while s3 implies ~140bp; and stale 0.946 density references remain against the 0.937 value. The 23.9% terminal ROE and the no-rights-issue base depend on this headroom.
challenges.answer: The capital estimate is now stated on the individual perimeter the floor is set on. Density 1.038 bridges consolidated attributable equity of Rp338.9tn to bank-only risk-weighted assets of Rp1,299.4tn at 20.62% individual KPMM, against Rp1,438.5tn and 22.99% consolidated [S15]. On the old plan path the individual-equivalent trough was 14.43% in FY2034E, through the floor, so loan growth now glides from FY2030E and the trough is 15.75% in FY2033E and 15.92% by FY2035E, about a percentage point of buffer. Payout stays at 92% and FY2026E DPS is unchanged at 379.29; dividend model 4,671 to 4,586, residual income 4,668 to 4,580, blend 4,385 to 4,324, target 4,250 to 4,188 and total return 62.0%, rating BUY. The 0.946 references are replaced and loan_growth, payout, terminal_growth and s3 now carry the same buffer arithmetic; the handoff 4,137 remains stale but the report is internally consistent at 4,188 [S15][S7].

missing_bull_case.note: The 92% payout at a 379.29 DPS on a 2,820 price is a 13.4% forward yield and the return anchor VAL_BANKS rule 5 defines for SOE banks, but it appears only as a capital risk. No scenario, bridge or sensitivity tests a special dividend or payout above 92% from the 5.9-8.3pp of capital above the 14.7% floor, and the second Rp1tn buyback is dismissed as signalling.

missing_bear_case.note: No NPL coverage ratio or provisioning-vs-write-off trend anywhere, which is the bank accruals test in EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS. The claim that the stock ratio rose because write-offs slowed is contradicted by F65, whose latest micro write-off is 5,312 against 4,385 prior, and loans at risk of 9.53% against gross NPL of 3.07% is quoted but never sized. The bear also cuts loan growth to 7%, which relieves the capital constraint the report names as a step-back trigger, and carries no rights issue or directed-lending shock.

assumption_realism.note: NIM 6.95% falling to 6.60% over seven years is about 8bp a year against a 37bp reported annual fall (6.53% to 6.16%), with no deposit-beta path in the model. Credit cost 3.2% is above the 9M 3.05%. And FY2026E equity of 334.08tn is below the actual 338.86tn at 30 September, so the ROE and CAR paths do not sit on the filing's book.

evidence_and_citations.note: Five load-bearing facts verified verbatim - S7 91.96% and Rp52.1tn, S4 Rp346 dividend, S9 7.45%, S10 1.62% spread and 2.46% CRP, S15 34.81tn impairment and 338.86tn parent equity. But section 1 lists the Rp53.68tn other-operating-income line as excluded from the pack's Rp50.03tn NOII when it is essentially that line, and 'government-subsidised' NTT relief, 'no pledged shares' and the index float are uncited.

valuation_method_fit.note: P/B, residual income and DDM are applied properly with one COE at 12.45%, a documented build and an explained divergence, and the Q3 parent equity is the anchor. But P/B primary at 50% contradicts VAL_BANKS rule 1 (residual income is the engine) without an argument, the blend sits below both cash-flow methods, and the equity roll, the PSAK 16 revaluation surplus and the bank net-debt bridge are unreconciled.

bias_and_tone.note: Prose is measured and the peer paragraph candid, but the target change is attributed to 'the share price over the same days' when the target construction is price-independent. 1.3x forward book appears against 1.28x in comps and 1.23x in the qc note, and 15.5% implied ROE is 14.6% below the 18.13% run-rate, not a fifth. 6,518 words against the 500-3,500 update range.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: COE 12.45%, terminal g 1.6% and the 12.80% BMRI rate read consistently with peers, and the AVOID NIM tilt is respected. But the deposit-beta and CASA path against the BI path is asserted, not modelled, and the macro deck is cited to news [S14][S17]; BRI also takes the lowest COE in the peer set (12.45 against BMRI 12.80) while carrying the highest credit cost.

conservatism_audit.note: Listed: FY2026E credit cost 3.2% against the 9M 3.05%, which requires a Q4 charge of 14.3tn, 23% above the 9M quarterly average, with no source; a CAR path starting at 22.0% against the reported 22.99%; a 4.6% bear, when the FY2021 stress was about 3.3%, weighted at 25%. Offsetting optimism: NIM compression at a fifth of the reported pace. The stack is worth roughly 3-5% of value and does not move the rating.

calibration.note: FY+1 ROE of 19.0% sits 1.31pp above FY2025A 17.7% with no qc_justification entry; on the 9M actual 18.13% and the Q3 opening equity the step is nearer 18.0%. FY2026E parent profit of 62.48tn is below the 9M annualised 63.6tn, defensible as Q4 seasonality but unsourced.

signoff.notes: L1 is closed on substance. Capital is now measured on the individual perimeter: rwa_density 1.038 = consolidated attributable equity to bank-only regulatory capital 338.9/267.9 = 1.265 x individual RWA to consolidated loans 1,299.4/1,583.8 = 0.820, which reproduces 20.61% against the reported 20.62% individual KPMM [S15 p10, F98/F132]; the consolidated-individual wedge was 2.41pp a year earlier against 2.37pp at September, so holding it fixed is evidenced. car_est runs 20.03% FY2026E to a 15.75% FY2033E trough and 15.92% FY2035E, 105bp above the 14.7% floor, and the buffer arithmetic is identical in assumptions (loan_growth, payout, terminal_growth), s3 and s5. The growth glide from FY2030E absorbs the constraint; payout stays 92% and FY2026E DPS is unchanged at 379; terminal ROE is 23.4%, below the 23.9% returned on. No live 0.937/0.946 values: the only two mentions are labelled earlier/superseded. The judge equity-roll BLOCK is rebutted arithmetically (324.03 + 62.48 - 31.68 - 20.76 = 334.08; the 20.61 interim sits in the opening book). The call is supported: warranted P/B 1.66x vs traded 1.28x, 13.4% forward yield, residual income 4,580 and DDM 4,586 above the 2,820 price, blend 4,324, weighted target 4,188, total return 62.0%. Residual watches for the next update, not challenges: fund record valuation.primary still reads justified_pbv though the weights are residual income 50%, P/B 30%, DDM 20% (a cosmetic vs-primary label); the 14.7% floor should be shown as derived 9.59-9.70% + 2.5% + 2.5%; and the fixed 2.37pp wedge is the main model risk, since a widening of more than 1pp would consume the 105bp buffer. No konglo. No broker or consensus material used.

bias.note: Base anchors on the last actual and is if anything conservative: credit cost 3.2% is above the 3.05-3.08% nine-month run-rate, NIM 6.95% is below the company's own 7.4-7.8% guidance, NOII growth 9.0% is below the 15.5% FY2025 and 9.4% three-year average, and terminal growth 1.6% is below the 1.9% retention funds at a 92% payout. Loan growth is the top of the raised 8-10% guide against +8.4% on the LK loans line in nine months [S14][S15]. The bear's 10% rights issue without proceeds is a sourced upper-bound stress, not the base. No unsourced haircut or optimism found in the base.

findings.finding: s4 says EPS, DPS and book value per share all use the 151,559,001,604 shares, but the P/B method's BVPS is 2,248.96, which is the 30 Sep 2026 parent book of Rp338.86tn divided by 150,674.1m net-of-treasury shares, not 151,559.0m. The model's own EPS/DPS/BVPS lines do use 151,559.0m. Target impact is about Rp25 (0.6% on the 30%-weighted P/B), no rating change [S15][S3].

The 14.7% capital floor is presented as the company reports. S15 p10 reports the components, not a 14.7% line: risk-profile-based CAR 9.59% (Sep-26) / 9.70% (Sep-25), capital conservation buffer 2.5% and systemic-bank surcharge 2.5%, i.e. 14.59-14.70%. The 11bp difference does not change the glide, which stays about 1pp above the floor [S15 p10].
s3 says deposits grow to Rp2,318.03tn so the LDR holds near 96.9%. 96.9% is the FY2026E LDR; on the model lines the LDR falls to 94.7% by FY2030E as deposits (+40%) outgrow loans (+37%).

The equity roll pays a lagged dps[-1], so the FY2026E deduction of Rp52.44tn is the FY2025 final (Rp31.68tn) plus a December-2026 interim implicitly held flat at Rp137/share (Rp20.76tn); the FY2026E book of Rp334.08tn foots on that convention. The engine does not split interim and final, so the convention is implicit. Also fund record valuation.primary is still justified_pbv (prior Q4) and orphan justifications drift.nim and scenario.symmetry.val.g remain in fund record.

The summary claim that the published target sat below every method is not true against the warranted P/B of Rp3,723, which is below the Rp4,010 v6 target; it was below residual income and DDM. The construction point stands without the overstatement [S15].

flags.message: a.credit_cost: bear 0.0125 vs bull -0.002 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bear adds 125bp to 4.6%, the credit cost consistent with the mid-teens perpetual return on equity the share price already discounts at a 12.45% cost of equity; the history of the last five years (3.33-3.39% in FY2024-25, roughly the FY2021 stress share) shows the downside can exceed that [S6][S4]. The bull subtracts only 20bp, to the 3.0% nine-month run-rate actually reported [S15], because the observed print - not a hypothetical trough - bounds the favourable case. The asymmetry is deliberate - the bull is anchored on a source, the bear is not bounded by one.

flags.message: a.share_change: bear 0.1 vs bull -0.0025 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bear models a 10% rights issue as a share-count increase without the cash proceeds, an upper-bound dilution for a bank that holds loan growth at the plan with a 92% payout and spends the buffer [S4][S7]. The bull's -0.25% is the announced Rp1tn second buyback tranche, about a quarter of one per cent of market capitalisation and the only capital return actually disclosed [S16]. They are not mirrored in size because a stress capital raise and a disclosed buyback are different events, not two settings of one driver; mirroring the 10% would assume a buyback ten times the announced tranche, which no source supports.

flags.message: dps FY2025A restated at 1.66x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack records only the Rp209 final tranche as FY2025 DPS; the full-year FY2025 dividend was Rp346 per share (interim Rp137 paid 15 Jan 2026 plus the final tranche) as the company states in its 1H26 presentation [S4] and as the April-2026 RUPST approved [S7].

flags.message: expected return +62%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The expected return is extreme because the price is. The three sourced drivers are credit cost normalising from the 3.33-3.39% of FY2024-25 [S6] to 3.2% in FY2026E on 1H26's 3.08% [S4]; a NIM that falls about 40bp over five years on a 12.2% loan yield and 2.4% cost of funds, against the 6.16% nine-month print [S4][S15]; and the revealed 92% payout held through the forecast [S7], with loan growth capped at the 1.6% retention funds once the estimated capital ratio reaches the 14.7% floor [S4]. At the market multiple of 1.28x FY2026E book (2,820 over 2,204 book value per share), a 12.45% COE and 1.6% growth, the price implies a perpetual return on equity of about 15.5%, against the 18.13% earned in the nine months to September - a shortfall of about one seventh [S15]. The bear case is shallower than that implied state, because at a 4.6% credit cost it still values the shares above the price, so the expected return is not produced by the bear. The reverse grid cannot bracket the price because the industry config searches only plus or minus 50bp of credit cost, so we state the implied return directly instead.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'justified_pbv': 0.5, 'residual_income': 0.3, 'ddm': 0.2}
flags.justification: The industry default weights are P/B half, residual income three tenths and DDM a fifth, but VAL_BANKS rule 1 makes residual income the engine for a bank; the report runs residual income at half, P/B at three tenths and DDM at a fifth, and the deviation is argued in section 4 [S15]. Keeping the default put the lowest of the three methods (P/B at 3,723 against 4,580 and 4,586) on half the weight, which is a construction error, not a market view.
